intro: Ladakh is a high, dry region between the Karakoram and the Great Himalaya, where Leh sits at about 3,500 metres and the passes rise above 5,000. The main adventure season runs from about June to September, when the roads from Manali and Srinagar are open and the rivers are high enough to raft. Winter brings a quieter season of frozen rivers, ice hockey and snow leopards.

Everything in Ladakh starts with acclimatisation. Plan at least two full days of rest in Leh before any strenuous activity, and more before going higher. This guide covers adventure activities; for routes, permits and a full itinerary, see our Leh Ladakh road trip guide.
quickAnswer: The best adventure activities in Ladakh are white-water rafting on the Zanskar and Indus rivers, treks such as Sham Valley, Markha Valley and the winter Chadar, motorcycle and road trips over Khardung La and Chang La to Nubra and Pangong, the Khardung La cycling descent, Bactrian camel rides at Hunder and camping by Pangong and Tso Moriri. The main season is June to September; rest two days in Leh first.
takeaways: Rest at least two full days in Leh before any strenuous activity.
Zanskar rafting from Chilling to Nimmu is Ladakh's classic white-water trip, from about June to August.
Sham Valley is an easy village trek; Markha Valley is a harder trek over a pass above 5,000 metres.
Road trips over Khardung La and Chang La link Leh with Nubra and Pangong.
Winter (January to March) is the season for snow leopard trips and the Chadar trek, conditions permitting.

sections.heading: Rafting on the Zanskar and Indus

items.name: Zanskar: Chilling to Nimmu
body: The run from Chilling to the Indus confluence near Nimmu passes through a deep gorge with Grade III to IV rapids in the high-water months. The water is glacial; wetsuits are provided.

items.name: Indus: Phey to Nimmu
body: A gentler Grade II to III stretch close to Leh, good for first-timers and families.

items.name: Sham Valley
body: An easy three- to four-day village walk west of Leh, via villages such as Likir, Yangthang, Hemis Shukpachan and Temisgam, with nights in homestays. A good acclimatisation trek.

items.name: Markha Valley
body: A six- to eight-day trek through Hemis National Park, crossing Kongmaru La at over 5,000 metres, with homestays and camps.

items.name: Chadar trek
body: The winter walk on the frozen Zanskar needs a medical check, insurance and permits in Leh, and depends entirely on the river freezing; it was suspended in January 2026.

image.alt: Trekkers on the frozen Zanskar river during the Chadar trek
image.caption: Chadar trek

items.name: Trekking peaks
body: Kang Yatse II from the Markha Valley and Mentok Kangri near Tso Moriri are 6,000-metre peaks climbed with experienced teams. Stok Kangri has been closed to climbers for periods; check its status.

items.name: Khardung La, Nubra and the Shyok road
body: The road north from Leh over Khardung La drops into Nubra Valley, and the Shyok road links Nubra with Pangong Tso. It is a classic three- to four-day loop by motorcycle or car.

items.name: Khardung La cycling descent
body: Operators drive riders to the pass and let them ride the long paved descent back towards Leh.

items.name: Changthang and the high lakes
body: The road to Tso Moriri and Tso Kar crosses the high Changthang plateau, and roads in the region reach extreme heights. Hanle, with its observatory and dark skies, is a stargazing destination.

items.name: Bactrian camel rides at Hunder
body: The sand dunes at Hunder in Nubra have two-humped Bactrian camels for short rides at sunset.

items.name: Lake camping at Pangong and Tso Moriri
body: Tent camps near the shores of Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri give a night at about 4,300 metres or higher. Very cold at night.

items.name: Winter wildlife and ice sports
body: From about January to March, naturalists lead trips to see snow leopards in areas such as Hemis National Park and the Sham region. Ice hockey is played on frozen ponds in Leh and villages in winter.

sections.heading: Acclimatisation plan
list: If you fly into Leh, rest completely on day one and take only short walks on day two.
Do gentle sightseeing around Leh (Shanti Stupa, Leh Palace, nearby monasteries) on days two and three.
Only then go over Khardung La or Chang La, and sleep in Nubra or at Pangong after that.
Drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol for the first days and eat light.
Talk to a doctor before the trip about altitude medication if you have any health concerns.

sections.heading: Permits and fees
paras: Indian citizens currently do not need an Inner Line Permit for most of Ladakh, though fees such as the environmental fee may apply. Foreign nationals need Protected Area Permits for areas such as Nubra, Pangong and Tso Moriri. Rules change, so check the Ladakh administration's current requirements, and see the permits section of our road trip guide.

safety: Never skip acclimatisation; altitude sickness is the biggest risk in Ladakh.
Descend immediately if you have severe headache, confusion, breathlessness at rest or loss of coordination.
Carry warm layers and sun protection; the sun is intense and nights are cold.
Do not drive or ride over the high passes late in the day.
Use registered rafting operators with wetsuits and safety kayaks.
Respect military areas and photography restrictions near the borders.
packing: Sunglasses with UV protection, high-SPF sunscreen and lip balm
Reusable water bottle (Leh has refill points)
A basic medical kit including altitude guidance from your doctor
Power bank; power cuts happen outside Leh

faqs.q: What are the best adventure activities in Ladakh?
faqs.a: Zanskar and Indus rafting, treks such as Sham Valley and Markha Valley, motorcycle trips over Khardung La, the cycling descent from Khardung La, camel rides at Hunder and camping by the high lakes.

faqs.q: When is the best time for adventure activities in Ladakh?
faqs.a: June to September for most activities; January to March for winter wildlife and, conditions permitting, the Chadar trek.

faqs.q: How many days should I rest in Leh before activities?
faqs.a: At least two full days, more before going higher than Leh.

faqs.q: Is river rafting in Ladakh difficult?
faqs.a: The Zanskar from Chilling to Nimmu has Grade III to IV rapids and cold water; the Indus from Phey to Nimmu is easier.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a permit for Ladakh?
faqs.a: Indian citizens currently do not need an Inner Line Permit for most areas, but fees may apply. Foreigners need Protected Area Permits. Check current rules.
